headline: High: kotaemon can expose sensitive documents to Prefect-driven workflows, creating default data-leakage and compliance risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests documents, HTML, MHTML, and chat transcripts, while prefect orchestrates workflows that can pass outputs onward. A shared filesystem or pipeline handoff could let attacker-controlled content in kotaemon influence prefect tasks. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this below high.
conditions: IF kotaemon outputs are written into a Prefect task input or shared workspace
IF Prefect tasks parse kotaemon-generated HTML, MHTML, or transcripts as instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff of raw document text between tools
Add a manual review step before Prefect consumes kotaemon outputs
Restrict shared workspace permissions to read-only where possible
Strip markup and prompt-like text before downstream parsing
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon touches documents, PDFs, XLSX, DOCX, chat transcripts, and API keys, and has broad network egress plus multiple API backends. Prefect is an orchestrator that can move workflow metadata and trigger external calls. If sensitive kotaemon content enters Prefect workflows, the pair can leak it beyond the original boundary by default.
conditions: IF kotaemon processes documents containing secrets or regulated data
IF Prefect workflows transmit task inputs or logs to external services
mitigations: Remove secrets from kotaemon inputs before orchestration
Turn off verbose task logging in Prefect
Use a local-only backend for any shared workflow data
Limit Prefect tasks to metadata, not raw document contents
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering at the workflow boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: kotaemon supports multiple instances and writes to ./ktem_app_data, while Prefect coordinates pipelines that may also mutate shared artifacts. The profiles do not show locking or isolated storage, so overlapping writes are plausible in default multi-instance deployments, though not proven high because Prefect's write surface is not explicit.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or artifact directory
IF Prefect tasks mutate files that kotaemon also updates
mitigations: Assign separate directories for each agent
Make shared artifacts read-only for one side
Run only one writer per dataset at a time
Check for file-lock support in the orchestrator
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon produces document-derived answers and citations, and Prefect is designed for orchestration and downstream action. If Prefect treats kotaemon output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into automated workflow steps. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Prefect uses kotaemon output as a task decision input
IF no validation step checks citations or extracted facts before execution
mitigations: Require human approval before actioning kotaemon outputs
Validate citations against source documents
Add schema checks on all handoff payloads
Log and compare outputs from a second retrieval pass
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating before orchestration

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon handles API keys and document content, while Prefect handles workflow metadata and can route data through external services. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if regulated documents or keys are logged or transported by Prefect. The profiles do not show HIPAA/GDPR certifications, so uncertainty escalates to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated documents or API keys are included in Prefect logs or task payloads
IF the deployment stores workflow data in a jurisdiction or retention regime different from the source data
mitigations: Redact secrets before workflow submission
Set short log-retention windows in Prefect
Keep regulated data out of workflow metadata
Review residency settings for any hosted backend
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class and residency routing
